question: The radii of two circles are 6 cm and 2 cm. The centers of the two circles are 10 cm apart. What is the length of a transverse common tangent?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Length of Transverse Common Tangent (TCT) = √(D² − (R + r)²)

⇒ TCT = √(10² − (6 + 2)²)

⇒ TCT = √(100 − 8²)

⇒ TCT = √(100 − 64) = √36

⇒ TCT = 6 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the smaller circle (r) = 2 cm

 PQ = Transverse Common Tangent

**Formula Used:**

Length of a transverse common tangent (TCT) = √(D² − (R + r)²)

**Calculation:**

⇒ TCT = √(10² − (6 + 2)²)

⇒ TCT = √(100 − 8²)

⇒ TCT = √(100 − 64)

⇒ TCT = √36

⇒ TCT = 6 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

A common tangent that does not cross the line segment joining the centers of the two circles. Formula: DCT = √(D² − (R − r)²).

Number of Common Tangents Rule

When the distance between centers D > R + r, there are exactly 4 common tangents (2 direct and 2 transverse). If D = R + r, the circles touch externally and have exactly 3 common tangents.
